Tuning must preserve the separation between model learning, calibration,
parameter selection and assessment. `calibrated_workflow()` accepts local Grid
and Bayes searches for binary, shared OvO/OvR, pairwise OvO and regression
procedures. This vignette builds on
`vignette("workflows", package = "vennabers")`; it additionally requires
`tune`, `dials` and `yardstick`. The deliberately small searches keep the
examples runnable during a package build; use larger budgets for real work.

## Data roles and search strategies

Reserve final assessment data first. When tuning calibration options, the
procedure also reserves selection rows S and final-fit rows F **within the
data supplied to fit**. S chooses calibration settings and never rejoins F.
Each model search sees only its permitted local training data, excluding its
VA calibration rows. Outer assessment is excluded from every inner operation.

| Strategy | Model-parameter criterion | Calibration selection |
|:---------|:--------------------------|:----------------------|
| `"joint"` | Score complete calibrated predictions | Select the complete procedure |
| `"two_stage"` | First score the raw model predictions | Then select calibration settings |

Both strategies keep the same data exclusions. Each Cross source model runs
its own local search. With `prediction_model = "full"`, the additional full
model runs its own search too; it does not inherit or average fold choices.

```{r data-and-recipe}
library(vennabers)
set.seed(19)
data <- data.frame(x = rnorm(800))
data$truth <- factor(ifelse(runif(800) < plogis(.5 * data$x),
                            "yes", "no"), levels = c("yes", "no"))
set.seed(20)
split <- rsample::initial_split(data, prop = .8, strata = truth)
development <- rsample::analysis(split)

recipe <- recipes::recipe(truth ~ x, data = development) |>
  recipes::step_poly(x, degree = tune::tune("degree"))
base <- workflows::workflow() |>
  workflows::add_recipe(recipe) |>
  workflows::add_model(parsnip::logistic_reg(engine = "glm"))

# Always construct resamples from the supplied local data.
folds <- function(data) {
  rsample::vfold_cv(data, v = 2, strata = truth, pool = 0)
}
```

`tune("degree")` names the parameter ID. Grid columns must match these IDs,
which must be unique across recipe, model and calibration settings. The ID
`id` is reserved by native tune. Never close over the full development data
inside a resampling callback.

## Joint Grid selection

Tune polynomial degree and the calibration regularization rule. There are
two model candidates and two calibration candidates. The primary criterion
here is Brier score for both searches, independent of the candidate loss rule.

```{r joint-grid}
config <- list(
  strategy = "joint",
  selection_prop = .3,
  model = list(method = "grid", grid = data.frame(degree = c(1L, 2L)),
               resamples = folds, primary_metric = yardstick::brier_class),
  calibration = list(method = "grid",
    grid = data.frame(va_loss = c("log", "brier")),
    resamples = folds, primary_metric = yardstick::brier_class)
)
tuned_spec <- calibrated_workflow(base, "truth", seed = 31,
  loss = tune::tune("va_loss"), tuning = config)
joint_fit <- generics::fit(tuned_spec, development)
choices <- venn_abers_tuning(joint_fit)
choices$calibration$selected
choices$models$Inductive1$selected
c(selection_rows = length(choices$calibration$selection_rows),
  final_fit_rows = length(choices$calibration$final_rows))
stopifnot(length(intersect(choices$calibration$selection_rows,
                           choices$calibration$final_rows)) == 0L)
```

By default classification searches use log loss (`yardstick::mn_log_loss`);
regression searches use RMSE. `report_metrics` adds reporting metrics without
changing the primary selection criterion. If you supply `control_grid()`,
set `save_pred = TRUE` so candidate completeness can be checked.

`venn_abers_tuning()` returns stored diagnostics without refitting: candidate
values, scores, eligibility and exclusion reasons, chosen settings, native
tune results, data roles and fit budgets. Ties use stable candidate order.
Inspect these records before treating a winning score as evidence.

## Two-stage Grid selection

Reuse the same candidate grids while changing which predictions guide the
model search:

```{r two-stage-grid}
two_stage <- config
two_stage$strategy <- "two_stage"
two_stage_spec <- calibrated_workflow(base, "truth", seed = 31,
  loss = tune::tune("va_loss"), tuning = two_stage)
two_stage_fit <- generics::fit(two_stage_spec, development)
venn_abers_tuning(two_stage_fit)$models$Inductive1$selected
venn_abers_tuning(two_stage_fit)$calibration$selected
```

The first stage now selects the raw model, before postprocessing or VA. The
second selects calibration. Neither strategy implies that a particular method
will win on future data. Choose between procedures using outer resampling or
separate validation, not the final assessment split.

To tune precision as well, use a distinct placeholder such as
`precision = tune::tune("va_rounding")` and a matching grid column. Precision
candidates are the strings `"none"`, `"0"`, `"2"` and `"-2"`; `"none"` means no
rounding. These categorical search values differ from fixed constructor
values such as `precision = NULL` or `precision = 2`.

## A small Bayes model search

Bayes searches require parameter definitions, positive `initial` and `iter`
budgets, and more initial candidates than tuned parameters. This model-only
example leaves calibration settings fixed, so no S/F selection split is
requested. A joint search still scores the complete calibrated procedure.

```{r bayes}
bayes_config <- list(
  strategy = "joint",
  model = list(
    method = "bayes", initial = 4L, iter = 1L,
    param_info = dials::parameters(list(degree = dials::degree_int(c(1L, 6L)))),
    resamples = folds,
    control = tune::control_bayes(seed = 4, save_pred = TRUE, uncertain = Inf)
  )
)
bayes_fit <- calibrated_workflow(base, "truth", tuning = bayes_config,
                                 seed = 31) |>
  generics::fit(development)
venn_abers_tuning(bayes_fit)$models$Inductive1$selected
```

The implementation advances native `tune_bayes()` one step at a time. Only
complete valid candidates inform the next Gaussian process; failed, dropped
and repeated proposals still spend iteration budget and count toward
`no_improve`. `uncertain = Inf` and saved predictions are required. Elapsed-time
limits are checked between complete steps. With calibration Bayes tuning,
also supply its `param_info`, resamples and one of `selection_prop` or
`selection_split`, just as for Grid selection.

## Outer resampling and final assessment

Resample the **unfitted outer specification**, so each analysis split reruns
the entire tuning, preprocessing, model and calibration procedure. Do not
calibrate once on all development data before resampling.

```{r outer-resampling}
set.seed(61)
outer_folds <- rsample::vfold_cv(development, v = 2, strata = truth, pool = 0)
evaluation <- tune::fit_resamples(
  tuned_spec, resamples = outer_folds,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::brier_class, yardstick::mn_log_loss),
  control = tune::control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE,
                                    pkgs = c("vennabers", "stats"))
)
tune::collect_metrics(evaluation)
tune::collect_notes(evaluation)
```

Review notes as well as metrics: a summary over only successful folds is not
a complete evaluation. Fix failed folds before comparing procedures. For
parallel outer resampling, make sure workers load `vennabers` and the required
engine namespaces. Inner search parallelism is disabled. Seed outer plans
separately from the constructor's local `seed`.

Here we preselect the joint Grid specification for demonstration. In an
application, compare candidate procedures using the outer results, freeze
that choice, and only then evaluate once on the held-out assessment split:

```{r final-assessment}
final <- tune::last_fit(
  tuned_spec, split = split,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::brier_class, yardstick::mn_log_loss)
)
tune::collect_metrics(final)
final_workflow <- tune::extract_workflow(final)
head(predict(final_workflow, rsample::assessment(split)["x"], type = "prob"))
```

Calibration selection continues to reserve S inside the analysis data; the
returned predictor fits only on F. Final assessment outcomes do not enter
either role. `last_fit()` is for a trainable specification, not a frozen
predictor from `calibrate_workflow()`.

## Extending the same pattern

For **regression**, use `m = tune::tune("moderation")` with a positive-integer
grid, or `epsilon = tune::tune("moderation")` with values strictly between zero
and one. Tune exactly one. Every local calibration fold must satisfy
`1 <= m <= floor((k - 1) / 2)`; epsilon determines m from that local size.
Invalid candidates are recorded and excluded, not clipped into range. Omit
classification loss and precision, and use unstratified numeric resampling.

For **shared OvO/OvR**, choose `classification` and a multiclass base model;
selection scores complete class vectors. **Pairwise OvO** uses local searches
inside each class pair. Its joint Grid path without postprocessing selects a
Cartesian grid of pair choices using `joint_resamples` and rejects more than
4096 combinations. Pairwise Bayes and tuned postprocessing search locally
instead; see `?venn_abers_tuning` before adapting a shared model plan.

With **postprocessing**, every B training portion runs its own local search,
excluding P (postprocessor), C (VA calibration), S (selection) and outer
assessment. Joint scoring evaluates complete compositions; two-stage scoring
starts from the raw engine. Postprocessing method, input and split strategy
stay fixed per search. Inspect local search counts and budgets because Cross,
pairwise training, ensembles and full-model transfer multiply the work.

Runnable larger examples are installed with the package:

```{r further-examples}
system.file("examples", c("regression-grid.R", "shared-multiclass-grid.R",
  "pairwise-grid.R", "postprocessing-grid.R", "postprocessing-bayes.R"),
  package = "vennabers")
```

For an already fixed classifier, a loss-only Log/Brier comparison does not
need automatic tuning or a refit: predict both losses on separate validation
rows, choose there, then pass the chosen `loss` explicitly on untouched
assessment data. Those validation rows are selection data from then on.

For the complete standalone scripts with a contents list, open
`vignette("examples-tuning", package = "vennabers")`.
`?vennabers_examples` indexes all four example collections.
